newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Arab-Malaysian sees softer property market.
newsitem.headline: Arab-Malaysian sees softer property market.

text.p: Malaysia's booming property sector might soften in one or two years because of excessive building activity, Arab-Malaysian group chairman Azman Hashim said.
"Of course, there are concerns about overbuilding. The market could be softening in one or two years' time," he told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
Malaysia's property sector been booming because the government has concentrated a lot of domestic activity around the construction industry.
The sector has also be helped by the country's booming economy, now in its ninth year of over eight percent growth.
A large number of other projects, including luxury hotels, shopping malls and sports complexes are aimed at the 1998 Commonwealth Games, which Malaysia is hosting.
Many analysts have said that demand for property might drop after the Commonwealth Games.
But Azman said if economic growth remained strong, as was expected, the downturn in property might not be severe.
"Domestically, prices may seem to have gone high, but (property is still) cheap compared to Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore," he said.
